neighbours.label: narrative moment of sudden distress or shock for a character (fear, grief, being overwhelmed)
fire: The door slammed behind her and the lights went out. With a sob, Mara pressed herself against the wall.
He read the letter twice, then sank to the floor, shaking with grief.
When the ice cracked beneath him, Tom screamed and clawed at the edge.
She found the empty crib and let out a terrible, choking cry.
Panic seized him as the smoke filled the narrow hallway.
The soldiers were overwhelmed with horror at what they found in the village.
Sick with dread, Elena watched the ambulance pull away without her son.
"Get away from me!" she shrieked, backing toward the broken window.
quiet: The door closed behind her and she switched on the lights. Mara hung her coat on the hook.
He read the letter twice, then folded it and put it in a drawer.
When the ice was thick enough, Tom laced his skates and glided out.
She found the crib in the attic and carried it downstairs.
He opened the window as the smell of bread filled the narrow hallway.
The soldiers were pleased with the supplies they found in the village.
Smiling, Elena watched the bus pull away with her son waving.
"Come over here," she said, walking toward the open window.
